articles.title: Capital Group sells 1% stake in D-Mart for Rs 2,537 crore
articles.description: Capital Group divested a 1.04 percent stake in Avenue Supermarts for Rs 2,537 crore. This significant open market transaction involved selling over 67 lakh equity shares of D-Mart's parent company. The shares were offloaded at an average price of Rs 3,750.58 per share. Avenue Supermarts' stock experienced a slight decline following the divestment announcement. The company recently reported an 11.33 percent rise in its June quarter net profit.

articles.title: Fed seen a bit more likely to hike after inflation data
articles.description: US inflation data showed a slight increase in July. The personal consumption expenditures price index rose to 3.7 percent. Core inflation remained unchanged, indicating persistent underlying pressures. This data strengthens the argument for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike. Traders now anticipate a higher probability of a September rate increase.

articles.title: US stocks today: US stocks slip at open after inflation data; Nvidia in focus
articles.description: US stocks opened lower on Wednesday after hotter-than-expected inflation data strengthened expectations of another Fed rate hike this year. articles.title: BSE, NSE impose over Rs 59 lakh penalty on NTPC, SJVN, REC for non-compliance
articles.description: The BSE and NSE have imposed financial penalties exceeding Rs 59 lakh on three public sector power companies: NTPC, REC, and SJVN. The fines are due to violations related to board composition listing regulations. In their defense, the companies argue that the appointment of directors falls under presidential powers. They are currently seeking waivers for these penalties.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Warren Buffett: "The inescapable fact is that the value of an asset, whatever its character, cannot over the long term grow faster than its earnings do"
articles.description: Warren Buffett’s investment philosophy emphasizes that an asset’s long-term value cannot sustainably outpace its earnings. articles.title: Sensex falls 183 points, Nifty closes below 24,250 as market erases all morning gains. What lies ahead?

articles.title: Dollar moves in a narrow range ahead of inflation data, Jackson Hole
articles.description: In Asian markets, the dollar held steady as traders looked ahead to crucial inflation reports, particularly the US PCE data set to be released before the Jackson Hole symposium this weekend. Meanwhile, oil prices dipped due to easing tensions in the Middle East and halted diplomatic negotiations. The Australian dollar strengthened following favorable inflation figures, while cryptocurrencies continued their upward trajectory, and gold saw a minor decline.

articles.title: Yes, Federal, RBL put dollar bond plans on hold
articles.description: Yes Bank withdrew its dollar debt plan as investors sought higher yields. Federal Bank and RBL Bank also postponed their dollar bond issuances. These lenders await a more favorable time to raise necessary foreign currency. An oversupply of Indian bonds has increased investor demand for better returns. This situation impacts the banks' ability to secure international funding.

articles.title: Gold little changed with US inflation data in spotlight
articles.description: Gold prices held steady as investors kept a watchful eye on upcoming United States inflation data, which is expected to offer insights into the Federal Reserve's interest rate decisions. Market participants are looking towards a potential pause in rate hikes next month. Concurrently, other precious metals, including silver, platinum, and palladium, experienced slight increases, reflecting ongoing global economic concerns and trade tensions impacting market dynamics.

articles.title: Oil prices slide 2% on Iran-Oman talks to reopen Strait of Hormuz
articles.description: Oil prices have dropped following the revival of discussions between Iran and Oman regarding the management of the Strait of Hormuz. The losses across both benchmarks highlight the market's reaction to navigation issues. Despite uncertainty gripping the market, some bargain buying has emerged, preventing further price decreases, while the U.S. is shifting personnel to its Middle Eastern diplomatic missions.

articles.title: Gross FDI climbs as net inflows turn positive
articles.description: Gross foreign direct investment into India saw a significant rise in June. Net FDI also increased substantially, recovering from a previous month's outflow. Outward FDI, however, continued its downward trend for the past two months. Financial, insurance, and business services were key sectors for outward investments. Manufacturing and trade sectors also witnessed outward FDI activity.

articles.title: Temasek-backed investor behind Unitree pitches Singapore as Chinese robots' path to U.S.
articles.description: As Washington shuts out Chinese robotics, a Temasek-backed VC bets that startups with genuine development in the city-state can still reach American buyers.

articles.description: Oil fell Wednesday, as investors continue to assess the U.S. pivot toward economic sanctions rather than military strikes to add pressure on Iran.

articles.title: 'Too much too quickly': Indonesia's growth ambitions questioned by economists
articles.description: Indonesia has set an ambitious growth target, but economists aren't sure it can get there while keeping the deficit in check.

articles.title: Outward remittances under LRS up at $2.5 billion
articles.description: In June, the total outward remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme soared to $2.5 billion. Notably, Indians disbursed $1.3 billion on international travel, reflecting a significant uptick from the previous month. Meanwhile, expenditure on overseas education rose to $96 million. Additionally, remittances for the upkeep of close relatives accounted for $287 million, while investments in equity and debt attracted $456 million from Indian residents.

articles.title: Axis Bank set to raise $700 million through ECB swap facility
articles.description: Axis Bank is set to secure seven hundred million dollars through a dedicated external commercial borrowing facility. This loan features two tranches with tenures of three and five years. The arrangement is spearheaded by CTBC Bank from Taiwan and United Overseas Bank from Singapore, with significant contributions from the World Bank's IFC. Additional banks are anticipated to participate as the syndication phase unfolds.

articles.title: Global Market Today: Asian stocks mixed ahead of Nvidia results, oil prices slide
articles.description: Contracts for the Nasdaq 100 Index dropped 0.3%, and those for the S&P 500 Index edged 0.1% down. MSCI’s Asia Pacific equities gauge was little changed with benchmarks in Japan and South Korea fluctuating between gains and losses.

articles.title: Rupee strengthens to 95.41 after oil cools
articles.description: The Indian rupee strengthened significantly on Tuesday, gaining 33 paise. This appreciation occurred as oil prices retreated and the Reserve Bank of India sold dollars. The rupee closed at 95.41, trading between 95.40 and 95.75 during the session. Oil prices fell more than three percent, influenced by US sanctions on Iran. Domestic markets will be closed Wednesday for a holiday.

articles.title: ESDS to expand data centre operations with Rs 720-cr IPO proceeds
articles.description: ESDS Software Solution is embarking on a ₹720-crore IPO aimed at broadening its data center operations across India and Europe. This strategic move follows a notable partnership for AI cluster deployment powered by NVIDIA GPUs. The investment will not only bolster their infrastructure but also pave the way for new facilities in Kolkata and Sahibabad, positioning ESDS as a trailblazer among India's publicly listed data center providers.

Anticipation builds for Wednesday as Groww gears up for a significant block deal, while Cipla faces new USFDA inspectional observations. In other news, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles is set to enhance its electric vehicle offerings through a collaboration with Tata Communications for 5G technology.

articles.title: D-Street set for a positive start as GIFT Nifty trades firmly higher
articles.description: The Nifty index recovered 0.5 percent, closing at 24,334 after touching a low. Positive global cues and FII buying supported this recovery ahead of expiry. Brent crude oil prices fell 3.2 percent, easing concerns about oil markets. The Indian rupee also strengthened by 24 paise against the US dollar. India VIX, a fear gauge, declined by 3.9 percent to 11.08 levels.

articles.title: Hindustan Copper OFS may not be a big draw for retail investors: Analysts
articles.description: Analysts express caution regarding retail investor interest in Hindustan Copper's offer for sale. A nearly ten percent discount may not attract investors after recent metal stock rallies. The institutional portion saw strong demand, exceeding shares available on the first day. Current valuations and limited upside potential raise concerns for potential subscribers. Investors are advised to seek better entry points in the secondary market.

articles.title: Small and midcaps shine as blue-chip stocks struggle for momentum
articles.description: Mid- and small-cap stocks have continued to defy index-level inertia amid a rush in primary-market listings. The average advance-to-decline (A/D) ratio - a widely watched indicator of overall market health - in August is up for the fifth consecutive month, its longest winning streak in more than two and a half years, pointing to significant investor interest beyond the typical frontbenchers that populate the two broadest gauges on the two competing exchanges.

Investors anticipate potential rate hikes later this year.

articles.description: The US Treasury will double its buyback operations for long-dated government debt. This move aims to provide liquidity and ease rising bond yields for investors. The increased buybacks will apply to securities maturing between ten and thirty years. This action follows a sharp bond selloff which pushed yields higher. The Treasury seeks to manage market pressures and borrowing costs effectively.

articles.title: Estee Lauder bets on fragrances and skincare to deliver strong annual profit
articles.description: Estee Lauder projects robust annual profits that are set to surpass Wall Street's expectations. The company's growth is heavily fueled by luxury fragrances, including popular lines such as Tom Ford and Le Labo. Estee Lauder anticipates an ongoing demand surge from young, affluent consumers while strategically broadening its brand presence in both China and international markets, aiming to enhance its makeup and hair care categories alongside its fragrances.

articles.title: SC rejects GST department review plea, telecom firms get relief on tower tax credit
articles.description: The Supreme Court rejected a review petition from the GST Department. This decision confirms telecom towers are movable property for tax credit. Bharti Airtel and Indus Tower received significant relief from this ruling. The court found no error in its previous order regarding tax eligibility. This reaffirms the principle of allowing credit for business inputs.

articles.title: RBI deputy governor Murmu calls for focus on meaningful financial inclusion
articles.description: Banks must measure financial inclusion by effective usage and informed decisions. Technology shifts and consumer behavior necessitate responsive banking systems. Digital inclusion deepens, and AI helps recognize capability across diverse groups. Institutions need skilled people to challenge models and oversee external providers. Prudence requires pooled intelligence and credible alternatives for system resilience.

articles.description: Indian monetary policy makers may tighten rates in the third quarter if inflation risks materialize. Higher food and fuel prices could lead to broad-based inflation, prompting action. Inflation is projected to peak at 5.9% in Q3 2026-27, signaling potential policy shifts. The central bank remains watchful of global economic turbulence and its domestic impact. Monetary response is warranted if inflation expectations become de-anchored or persistent.
